chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who freed a man, whose guardianship (wilāyah) is he? He said: 'For the one who freed him, if he has no heir other than her.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the guardianship of a freed slave if the woman who freed him has other heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance of *wilāyah* (guardianship) for a freed slave, establishing that the female manumitter retains this right unless she has other heirs, in which case it passes to them. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that *wilāyah* is treated as a financial right (*haqq mali*) that can be inherited, ensuring the freed slave remains under the protection of the manumitter's family line.
